SCHOOL ROOM · HOLIDAYS & SPECIAL DAYS · AGES 2–5

The School Hall — where the whole school celebrates.

Welcome to the Hall! In a real school this is the room where everybody gathers — for assemblies, for parties and for the special days on the calendar. Below is our big calendar of holidays: the next one comes first. Pick it, print its cards, and get ready together.

Explore the other rooms ↗
COMING UP · THE SCHOOL CALENDAR

The next holiday first.

Five special days a year, always in date order, always starting with the next one — so this room never looks empty and never goes quiet.

  1. Sat 31 Oct 2026 · coming up nextHalloween

    Dress up, say boo, carve a friendly pumpkin.

  2. Thu 26 Nov 2026Thanksgiving

    A big dinner and a thank-you list, together.

  3. Fri 25 Dec 2026Christmas

    Lights, songs, presents and the family table.

  4. Sun 14 Feb 2027Valentine’s Day

    Little cards that say “I like you.”

  5. Wed 10 Mar 2027Eid

    New clothes, sweet treats and “Eid Mubarak!”

Dates for Halloween, Thanksgiving (the fourth Thursday in November), Christmas and Valentine’s Day are fixed; Eid dates are expected dates — the moon decides, so check with your family’s calendar.

WHY A HALL

Assemblies, parties and celebrations — kid-sized.

Every holiday page in the Hall is spoken straight to kids: what the day is, why people celebrate it, and things a two-to-five-year-old can actually do — make a card, dance, count pumpkins, taste something new. Grown-ups get the how-to notes in small print beside each idea, and every printable in the Hall downloads and prints free, straight from its holiday page, with a print button that runs one card at a time.

AROUND THE SCHOOL

Where the Hall joins the school day.

Seasons in Class 34 · Ages 4–5 ↗Holiday crafts in the Art Room · Ages 2–5 ↗All the school rooms ↗

The Hall sits beside the school’s everyday rooms: Class 34 watches the seasons turn outside the window, and the Art Room keeps the glue and crayons a holiday craft needs. When the calendar says a special day is near, start there, craft here — and celebrate in the Hall.

Special days are how children mark time. One calendar, five celebrations, a room that stays useful all year — that is the Hall.
